extracted.intended_audience: science journalists, research institutions' communications/PR staff, PR firms, and researchers interested in press-release ethics
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for ethical handling of scientific press releases and embargo practices, aimed at improving accuracy, fairness, and transparency in science PR and journalism. Covers embargo handling, accuracy/claim standards, and examples of spin or misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embargo respected / embargo violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Embargo violations across science journalism (press releases and coverage should honor agreed embargo times).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track and penalize outlets that publish before the agreed embargo lift; treat early publication as an ethical breach. Examples/anti-patterns include outlets breaking embargos and 'soft' or informal embargoes that are not enforced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selective lifting / unfair early access
rubrics_metrics.description: Selective lifting where one outlet is given early access unfairly (not all outlets receive the embargoed materials simultaneously).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fair access requires providing the same materials and timing to all invited outlets; giving exclusive early access creates inequity and undermines embargo integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soft embargoes (informal sharing)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Soft embargoes' where information is shared but not formally embargoed, creating ambiguity about allowed publication timing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid informal arrangements that create confusion; clearly state embargo terms and expectations. Soft embargoes lead to disputed publication timing and perceived favoritism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embargo broken by overseas outlets
rubrics_metrics.description: Embargoes broken by overseas outlets (time-zone or jurisdiction issues leading to premature publication by international media).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate time-zone differences when setting lift times (specify timezone like PT/ET) and ensure consistent distribution so overseas outlets understand local lift timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source–PR firm coordination breakdowns
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordination breakdowns between study authors/sources and the PR firm leading to premature or inaccurate releases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain clear, documented communication channels and sign-off procedures between authors and PR firms to prevent inadvertent leaks or inaccuracies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embargo with no exclusivity offered
rubrics_metrics.description: Embargos issued without offering any exclusivity (i.e., no exclusive story window to any outlet).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify whether embargo implies any exclusive access; if exclusivity is part of the agreement, state terms explicitly. If not, ensure fair simultaneous distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear lift time (timezone-specified)
rubrics_metrics.description: Embargo lift time is stated clearly in PT/ET (or other timezone).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always give a specific lift time including timezone (e.g., PT/ET) so all outlets know exactly when publication is permitted; ambiguous times encourage violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance materials timing (48–72 hours)
rubrics_metrics.description: Materials should be sent 48–72 hours before the embargo lifts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide press materials within this window to allow journalists time to evaluate the paper and prepare accurate coverage; too-short windows increase risk of superficial or inaccurate reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fair access across outlets
rubrics_metrics.description: Fair access across outlets — do not give some outlets preferential early access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distribute materials equitably; document recipient lists and timing to defend against claims of favoritism and to maintain a level playing field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honor revoked for violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Agreed penalties or revocation of privileges for outlets that violate embargo terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State and (if necessary) enforce consequences for embargo violations (e.g., revoking future embargo access) to uphold norms and deter breaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author availability confirmed
rubrics_metrics.description: Confirm that study authors will be available to speak to press around the embargo lift.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure authors can be reached for comment at lift time to allow journalists to seek clarifications and independent perspectives; lack of availability increases risk of incomplete or misleading coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclusions must match the underlying paper
rubrics_metrics.description: Press-release conclusions should match the findings and claims of the underlying scientific paper exactly (no stronger claims than supported).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overstating significance or certainty; paraphrase paper conclusions accurately. Anti-patterns include overreach and claim inflation relative to the actual results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid causal claims when only correlation exists
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not state causal relationships if the underlying study only demonstrates correlation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully check study design and language; use cautious phrasing ('associated with', 'correlates with') when appropriate. Misrepresenting correlation as causation is a common inaccuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect sizes reported fully (relative and absolute)
rubrics_metrics.description: Effect sizes should be given as both relative and absolute measures (not only relative percentages).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide absolute risks or differences alongside relative changes to give readers a clearer sense of real-world impact; omitting absolute figures can mislead or exaggerate perceived effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: No cherry-picked subgroup analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid highlighting subgroup analyses selectively when they are not the primary, pre-specified findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag and contextualize subgroup results (e.g., exploratory nature, limited power). Cherry-picking subgroups to create a stronger narrative is misleading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology summary provided
rubrics_metrics.description: Press releases should include a summary of methodology (how the study was done).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include design, sample size, key methods, and limitations in brief to allow readers and journalists to assess the robustness of the findings; missing methodology details are a common flaw.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations explicitly noted
rubrics_metrics.description: Limitations of the study must be explicitly noted in the press release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State key caveats (sample size, model limitations, observational design, generalizability) plainly. Omitting limitations is a hallmark of spin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer external expert contacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide contact details for external experts who can comment independently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List neutral external experts so journalists can obtain independent perspectives; relying solely on the authors for comment reduces critical viewpoint and increases promotional tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid implying clinical relevance from preclinical work
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not imply that preclinical (e.g., cell/animal) findings have direct clinical relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly distinguish preclinical vs. clinical stages and avoid language that suggests imminent human benefit when none is supported by the study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid hyping early-stage research
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not hype results from early-stage or preliminary studies beyond what they warrant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contextualize early findings, note next steps and uncertainty; hype increases public misunderstanding and may fuel unwarranted expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide external validation or context (quote external experts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include quotes or perspectives from independent experts, not only study authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: External expert commentary helps contextualize findings and reduces perceived promotional bias of author-only quotes; anti-pattern: quoting only the study authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone parity with the paper (avoid over-enthusiasm)
rubrics_metrics.description: Press-release enthusiasm should not exceed the paper's tone (the release should not be more enthusiastic than the paper).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure press-release language reflects the study's actual strength and limitations; overenthusiastic press copy amplifies spin and misleads readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor industry vs. academic press-release quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Track and compare differences in press-release quality between industry-issued and academic-institution-issued releases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that motivations differ (e.g., commercial interests); evaluate releases with attention to potential conflicts of interest, promotional slant, and omitted information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track patterns of selective fact disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Watch for patterns where some facts are withheld or selectively presented to shape narratives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify recurring omissions or selective emphasis (e.g., leaving out negative results or key limitations) as indicators of systematic spin or unethical PR practices.
